newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-KLESKO HOMERS TWICE AS BRAVES BLAST ROCKIES.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-KLESKO HOMERS TWICE AS BRAVES BLAST ROCKIES.

text.p: Ryan Klesko homered twice and Greg Maddux got his sixth straight win, becoming the National League's first 13-game winner as the Atlanta Braves handed the Colorado Rockies their sixth consecutive loss Thursday, 8-2.
Klesko hit a solo shot off starter Bill Swift (4-3) in the bottom of the fourth and a two-run blast off Mike DeJean in a four-run seventh.
"I've been feeling better at the plate the last couple of weeks," he said. "I need to have a few good games in a row, get back to where I want to be."

Maddux (13-3) allowed two runs and seven hits with a walk and three strikeouts. The four-time Cy Young Award-winner has not lost since June 13 and is 6-0 with a 2.93 ERA since then. Maddux also stole a base after singling in the sixth.
"I didn't think a three-run lead was enough. I figured it was a good time to run. They weren't holding me on, I figured why not take a chance," he said.
"They've got a guy who hits .400 (Larry Walker), lots of power and they lead the league in runs scored. It's never over with them. You know they can break out any inning, any game."
"He didn't have his absolutely best stuff, but he made some absolutely great pitches," Braves manager Bobby Cox said of Maddux.
Eddie Perez also homered and Andruw Jones added two hits and two RBI for the Braves, who have won three of their last four games.
Walker and Vinny Castilla homered for the Rockies, who suffered their eighth straight road loss and fell to 1-13 in July. "I'm beyond embarrassed," manager Don Baylor said.
In Houston, Mark Gardner (10-4) allowed a run and five hits over eight innings and Barry Bonds scored twice as the San Francisco Giants beat the Astros 3-1.
Rod Beck worked a 1-2-3 ninth to earn his major league-leading 30th save for the Giants, who had lost three of their last four games.
Astros starter Chris Holt (7-6) gave up two runs over six innings.
At Florida, Al Leiter allowed two runs over six innings and Edgar Renteria had three hits and two RBI as the Marlins held off the Los Angeles Dodgers 8-7.

Leiter (8-6) gave up five hits, walked three and struck out eight. Robb Nen picked up his 25th save, despite allowing home runs to Tripp Cromer and Eric Karros in the ninth. Rookie centre fielder Mark Kotsay made a diving catch on Tom Prince's line drive to end the game with the tying run on first base.

Gary Sheffield and Luis Castillo each had two RBI for Florida, which has won six of seven games from Los Angeles this season. Charles Johnson added three hits and tied a Marlins record with four runs.
Tom Candiotti (5-3) took the loss.

In Pittsburgh, Hal Morris had three hits and tied a career high with five RBI and John Smiley struck out eight in seven innings to post his third straight victory as the Cincinnati Reds stopped the Pirates 9-5.
Smiley (8-10) allowed three runs and eight hits and is 5-6 lifetime against his former team. Francisco Cordova (6-6) took the loss.

Bret Boone had four hits and drove in two runs for the Reds, whose third through seven hitters -- Jon Nunnally, Willie Greene, Morris, Joe Oliver and Boone -- went 15-for-22 as the Reds pounded out a season-high 17 hits.
In St. Louis, Joey Hamilton and Trevor Hoffman combined on a seven-hitter and Steve Finley hit a two-run homer, powering the San Diego Padres past the Cardinals 3-1.

Hamilton (8-3) allowed one run and seven hits in eight-plus innings, leaving after Gary Gaetti led off the ninth with a single. Hoffman retired all three batters he faced, striking out two, for his 21st save.
Ex-Padre Andy Benes (6-4) gave up three runs and five hits in seven innings. He has just one win in his last seven starts.

San Diego's Tony Gwynn went 2-for-4, including an RBI double in the fifth, and is batting .398. His eighth-inning single was the 2,707th hit of his career, moving him past Doc Cramer into 50th place on the all-time list.

In New York, Butch Huskey's career-high fourth hit of the game -- a two-out single in the bottom of the 10th -- scored Edgardo Alfonzo with the game-winning run as the Mets edged the Chicago Cubs 4-3.
Huskey is 12-for-25 (.480) with three homers and nine RBI in his last seven games.

Backup catcher Todd Pratt had three hits and two RBI for New York, which snapped a three-game losing streak. John Franco (2-1), who pitched a 1-2-3 top of the 10th, picked up the win. Kent Bottenfield (1-2) took the loss.

In Philadelphia, Mike Lansing, Chris Widger and Rondell White homered and Carlos Perez came within one out of his sixth complete game as the Montreal Expos held on for a 5-4 victory over the Phillies.
Perez (9-4) exited after surrendering a two-run homer to Rico Brogna. Ugueth Urbina struck out Mike Lieberthal for his 17th save.
